subject: Benchmark onboarding checklist & kickoff asks
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Ellis Moore <ellis.moore@clearbox.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Benchmark onboarding checklist & kickoff asks

Hi Ellis / Jo —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the things we need from ClearBox to get a reproducible qualification run scheduled: 

- SLO targets you mentioned (please confirm final numbers): p95 latency target ~150 ms, p99 target ~500 ms; streaming start-to-first-token target ~80 ms; per-token sustain ~120 tokens/sec in streaming mode. Concurrency baseline for initial runs: 100 concurrent connections, with the ability to scale to 200 in a later soak.
- Typical request shapes: average prompt length ~320 tokens, 95th percentile prompt length ~1,200 tokens. Please share a representative payload and the expected distribution if possible.
- Prompt bundle: a seed set (prompt_seed_bundle.zip) and a canonical test harness input file. If you can share by EOD Wed 9/16 that would be ideal.
- Environment: confirm whether the tests should run against Redwood Hosted or your VPC Private deployment (we need network details if VPC).
- Security docs: we can share SOC2 artifacts and the minimal compliance checklist you requested; will include a link in the guide.

Measurement / reproducibility items we recommend including from our side:
- Warm-up: 2 minute warm-up window before measurements; 5-minute steady-state window for throughput measurements.
- Streaming: define start-to-first-byte (SFFB) as time from request acceptance to first token emitted by the model. For token throughput, measure tokens/sec after SFFB over the steady-state window.
- Cache priming: indicate whether prefix caching / KV cache is allowed; if so, provide representative cache keys or instructions to prime.

Attached: discovery_notes_20260910.pdf (summary of call). I will also share our benchmark guide and a short harness template separately.

Proposed next steps: 
1) You share prompt bundle + payload samples by EOD 9/16.
2) We exchange harness config and pin model variant.
3) Kickoff run (remote) — propose Thu 9/16 10:00 PT for a 45-minute kickoff to walk through the harness and initial results.

Would you like that time?

Thanks —
Lauren

Hi Lauren —

Thanks for this clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Targets: we can confirm p95 <= 150 ms and p99 <= 500 ms for the initial qualification. Streaming SFFB target 80 ms is OK for now; sustained per-token rate we expect ~120 tokens/sec typical, spikes up to ~200 tokens/sec for batch transcript scenarios.
- Concurrency: let’s start with 100 concurrent clients for the qualification run; we will request a separate soak at 200 concurrent next quarter.
- Prompt bundle: we will drop the seed bundle in a shared S3 link by EOD 9/16. It will include ~1,000 prompts with metadata (avg/95/long tail flags).
- Environment: we prefer the run to execute in our VPC (security policy). We will provide a test subnet + temporary IAM role; please confirm Redwood’s VPC runbook and any dependencies (KMS/HSM access, egress rules).

On reproducibility/measurement: can Redwood publish the harness code (or an immutable hash) and a script to set RNG seeds and deterministic tokenization? We need to be able to reproduce runs on our side later. Also: how do you account for network time vs. server-side decode time in your numbers?

I’ll loop in our infra contact if needed once we have the runbook.

Best,
Ellis
Ellis Moore
Head of Platform Engineering | ClearBox Health
ellis.moore@clearbox.ai

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Ellis Moore <ellis.moore@clearbox.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Benchmark onboarding checklist & kickoff asks

Ellis — good questions. Below are concrete measurement definitions and reproducibility steps we’ll follow; I’ve attached our short benchmark guide for reference (redwood-benchmark-guide_v1.md) and a Drive link with the harness artifacts.

Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/clearbox/bench-harness-202609 (access granted)

Measurement definitions (what we will report):
- Latency: server-side decode time measured at the inference host (time from model invocation to token emit) and client-observed latency (time from request to final token receipt). We’ll report p50/p95/p99 for both. Network time will be reported separately so you can subtract network RTT if needed.
- Streaming SFFB: measured as time from request ingress at our edge to the first token arriving at the client. We’ll publish both edge-to-client and host decode contributions.
- Token throughput: measured as tokens/sec over a 5-minute steady-state window after warm-up; we’ll include both aggregate and per-connection distributions.
- Concurrency/soak: runs will ramp over 3 minutes to the target concurrency, hold for configured soak duration (default 10 minutes), then ramp down. Warm-up period of 2 minutes precedes measurement windows.
- Determinism: harness will accept a seed parameter and fixed tokenizer version. We’ll publish the harness repo commit hash and a SHA256 of the input prompt bundle used.

Operational notes:
- Cache priming: we will provide a priming script if you opt to test with prefix/KV caching enabled; if not, we’ll run cold-start tests. Please specify which modes you want included in the report.
- Model variant: for deterministic comparisons we suggest starting with redwood-r1.2-8bit as a baseline; if you have constraints we can switch.
- Artifacts we’ll share after each run: raw harness logs, token-level timing CSV, harness commit hash, and a canonical results summary.

Proposed kickoff time still Thu 9/16 10:00 PT — please confirm and we’ll send an invite with a short agenda (walk harness, confirm env, run a quick smoke).

Regards,
Lauren

Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Benchmark harness config (proposal)

Team —

Attaching the harness config we plan to use for the kickoff qualification. Highlights:
- model: redwood-r1.2-8bit (pinned commit)
- seed: 20260913-CLR (harness seed param)
- warmup: 120s, steady_state: 300s
- concurrency ramp: linear 0->100 over 180s, soak 600s default (we will shorten to 300s for the initial demo)
- streaming mode: enabled; measure SFFB + tokens/sec after first token
- metrics: server_decode_ms, client_observed_ms, tokens_per_second, error_rate

Attachments included: harness_config.yaml, run_template.sh

Please review — I want to confirm quantization and whether we should test an 8-bit vs 4-bit variant in the first run. My recommendation: 8-bit baseline for latency/throughput parity.

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
